### Introduction:

Special thanks to: https://github.com/justmarkham for sharing the dataset and materials.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justmarkham/DAT8/master/data/u.user).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called users.

```{r}
users <- read_delim("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justmarkham/DAT8/master/data/u.user",
                    delim = "|")
head(users)
```

### Step 4. Discover what is the mean age per occupation

```{r}
users |>
  group_by(occupation) |>
  summarise(age = mean(age))
```

### Step 5. Discover the Male ratio per occupation and sort it from the most to the least

```{r}
# create a function
gender_to_numeric <- function(x) {
  if_else(x == "M", 1, 0)
}

# apply the function to the gender column and create a new column
users <- users |> mutate(gender_n = gender_to_numeric(gender))

users |>
  group_by(occupation) |>
  summarise(male_ratio = sum(gender_n) / n() * 100) |>
  # sort to the most male
  arrange(desc(male_ratio))

# shorter: the mean of a logical vector is the proportion of TRUE values
# users |> summarise(male_ratio = mean(gender == "M") * 100, .by = occupation)
```

### Step 6. For each occupation, calculate the minimum and maximum ages

```{r}
users |>
  group_by(occupation) |>
  summarise(min = min(age), max = max(age))
```

### Step 7. For each combination of occupation and gender, calculate the mean age

```{r}
users |>
  group_by(occupation, gender) |>
  summarise(age = mean(age), .groups = "drop")
```

### Step 8. For each occupation present the percentage of women and men

```{r}
# count each combination of occupation and gender
users |>
  count(occupation, gender) |>
  # divide each count by the total of its occupation and multiply by 100
  group_by(occupation) |>
  mutate(percentage = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
  ungroup()
```
